elements.texte:
[cheerful] A courier delivers orders the same day, only in Paris.

Logistics wants to give them the processing orders of its Paris customers.

We get the ID and status of the orders from the orders table,

And the customers’ first name, last name and city from the customers table.

So we need to link the two tables, under certain conditions.

elements.texte:
[cheerful] We add a second condition with and, right after the first one.

For each pair, the ON now checks two conditions.

First condition: does order number 13 belong to the customer Sophie Martin?

Order number 13 has customer underscore ID equals 1, and Sophie Martin has ID equals 1.

The IDs match: the condition is true.

Second condition: does Sophie Martin live in Paris? Yes, her city is Paris.

With and, both conditions must be true: so the order appears in the result.

If Sophie Martin lived in Lyon, this row would be left out.

Don’t mix them up: 13 is the order’s ID, 1 the customer’s.

Order number 14 and Emma Dubois: she’s its customer, but she lives in Marseille.

A single false condition is enough: the two rows are not linked.
